title: Refractive Surgery: Modern Frontiers & Clinical Standards
summary: A comprehensive deep-dive into the current landscape of refractive surgery, integrating advanced laser platforms, phakic intraocular lenses, and cutting-edge biomechanical screening. This guide synthesizes evidence from the latest clinical abstracts and the AAO BCSC guidelines for the modern ophthalmic surgeon.

sections.title: Core Definition & Scope
sections.content: Refractive surgery encompasses a spectrum of surgical procedures designed to modify the refractive state of the eye, reducing or eliminating dependency on spectacles or contact lenses. This includes keratorefractive (laser and non-laser), phakic intraocular lenses (pIOLs), and refractive lens exchange (RLE). The goal is to alter the cornea's curvature or the eye's internal optics to bring light to a precise focus on the fovea.

sections.title: Comprehensive Pre-Operative Workup
content: 1. Manifest & Cycloplegic Refraction (Goal: < 0.5D difference)
2. Corneal Tomography (Pentacam/Galilei): Elevation & Pachymetry
3. Epithelial Thickness Mapping (ETM): Identifying early keratoconus masking
4. Biomechanical Analysis (Corvis ST / ORA): Measuring corneal hysteresis
5. Pupillometry: Photopic, Mesopic, and Scotopic diameters
6. Ocular Surface Disease (OSD) Screening: TBUT, Schirmer, Meibography
7. Fundus Exam: Peripheral retinal screening for lattice/tears (esp. myopes)

sections.title: Absolute Contraindications
content: Clinical Keratoconus or Ectasia
Unstable Refraction (>0.5D change in 12 months)
Active Herpetic Keratitis or Ocular Infection
Severe Dry Eye Disease (uncontrolled)
Connective Tissue Diseases (SLE, Rheumatoid Arthritis with active melt risk)
Pregnancy / Nursing (hormonal refractive shifts)
Unrealistic Patient Expectations

sections.title: LASIK Step-by-Step Surgical Technique
content: 1. Flap Creation: Femtosecond laser (approx 90-110μm thickness)
2. Flap Lift: Meticulous edge dissection and folding
3. Stromal Ablation: Excimer laser (193nm) with active eye-tracking
4. Interface Irrigation: Removing debris/epithelial cells
5. Flap Repositioning: Alignment using marks, ensuring 'no-striae' fit
6. Edge Drying: Ensuring adhesion via capillary action (approx 2 mins)

sections.title: Recent Advances & Landmark Studies
content: PROWL-1 & PROWL-2 Trials: Confirmed high satisfaction (>95%) and clarified 'visual symptoms' vs 'visual dissatisfaction'.
Ray-Tracing Guided Ablation: Uses a virtual eye model (Innovision) to account for axial length and internal optics, surpassing wavefront-optimized outcomes.
Evo+ ICL with KS-AquaPORT: Eliminated the need for Peripheral Iridotomy (PI), significantly reducing the risk of pupillary block and Uveitis-Glaucoma-Hyphema syndrome.
SMILE Pro (Visumax 800): Reduced suction time to <10 seconds and integrated centration and cyclotorsion compensation.
Corneal Allogenic Intrastromal Ring Segments (CAIRS): Using donor stromal tissue for keratoconus to improve biocompatibility over PMMA rings.

sections.title: Presbyopia Correction Strategies
content: Monovision (Blended Vision): Dominant eye for distance, non-dominant for near (-1.0 to -1.5D).
Presby-LASIK (Supracor/Presbyond): Creating a multifocal corneal profile.
Scleral Microporation (Laser): Softening the sclera to improve accommodative amplitude (Experimental).
Pharmacological: Miotic drops (Pilocarpine 1.25%) to increase depth of focus via pinhole effect.

sections.title: Landmark Clinical Pearls
content: The 'Golden Rule' of Residual Stromal Bed (RSB): Maintain >250μm (preferably >300μm) to prevent ectasia.
PTA (Percent Tissue Altered): Keep PTA <40% for LASIK; calculation: (Flap + Ablation) / Central Pachymetry.
Hyperopic Shift: Commonly seen in post-RK patients decades later; management involves CXL or Scleral lenses.
SMILE Lenticule Thickness: Minimum 10-15μm for easy manual dissection; too thin leads to tearing.
CXL-Plus: Combining Cross-linking with Topo-guided PRK is the standard for visual rehabilitation in stable Keratoconus.
